newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania workers protest against layoffs.
newsitem.headline: Romania workers protest against layoffs.

text.p: Romanian industrial workers, fearing layoffs, demonstrated in several cities on Wednesday to urge the centrist government to speed up reforms and ensure job security.
"We are starving and you earn millions" and "Thieves, thieves" shouted about 500 Bucharest workers as they marched past the Senate headquarters in heavy rain.

The rallies, called by the National Union Bloc (BNS), one of the biggest trade union federations, were the latest in a series of protests over tough economic reforms launched by the government in February.

Over 1,000 workers demonstrated in the Transylvanian city of Cluj, while traffic was halted in the northwestern city of Oradea when protesters drove through in about 100 trucks, local journalists said.

"We are not pleased with the way reforms are implemented," Nicolae Morgovan, head of Oradea's BNS branch, told protesters. "We want safe jobs. We don't want the social cost of the reform to be so high."

The reforms have brought hardships, including high prices and unemployment, to the already impoverished population. Average monthly pay is now around $80 and official data shows that purchasing power has halved since the 1989 collapse of communism.
The centrist government, which ousted ex-communists in last November's elections, has pledged to speed up reforms and perform the radical surgery needed to restore economic health.
